description: Per account scope, average the net fee rate over every fee record and count fee records.

b.request: For each account scope, join fees to orders and orders to users using the specified keys, discard unmatched rows, and report the scope, the unrounded average of `fees.feerate - fees.rebrate` across fee records, the number of fee records averaged, and that average minus the unweighted mean of all scope averages
b.sql: WITH scope_fees AS (SELECT u.acctscope AS scope, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(*) AS fee_record_count FROM fees AS f INNER JOIN orders AS o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault INNER JOIN users AS u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT scope, avg_net_fee_rate, fee_record_count, avg_net_fee_rate - AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) OVER () AS difference_from_scope_mean FROM scope_fees ORDER BY scope;

a.request: For each account scope (`users.acctscope`), taking fee records linked to their order (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`) and that order's user (`orders.userlink` = `users.userstamp`), and dropping any without a match, show the scope, the average net fee rate (`feerate` minus `rebrate`) taken over individual fee records (ignoring records where it is missing), the number of fee records, and how far the scope's average net rate is above or below the plain average of the per-scope averages. No rounding.
a.sql: WITH scope_fees AS (SELECT u.acctscope, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(*) AS fee_record_count FROM fees AS f JOIN orders AS o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users AS u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, avg_net_fee_rate, fee_record_count, avg_net_fee_rate - AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) OVER () AS difference_from_scope_average FROM scope_fees ORDER BY acctscope

c.request: For each account scope, using fees tied to orders (`fees.orderslink` = `orders.recordvault`) and to the users who placed them (`orders.userlink` = `users.userstamp`), with unmatched rows dropped, show the scope, the average net fee rate (fee rate minus maker rebate rate), how many it was averaged over, and how far that average sits from the simple mean of the scope averages. Don't round. Per account scope, average the net fee rate over every fee record and count fee records.
c.sql: WITH scope_fees AS (SELECT u.acctscope AS scope, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate, COUNT(*) AS fee_count FROM fees AS f INNER JOIN orders AS o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault INNER JOIN users AS u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT scope, avg_net_fee_rate, fee_count, avg_net_fee_rate - AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) OVER () AS difference_from_mean_scope_average FROM scope_fees ORDER BY scope

d.request: For each account scope, join fees to orders on `fees.orderslink = orders.recordvault` and orders to users on `orders.userlink = users.userstamp`, dropping unmatched rows. Across every matching fee record, calculate the unrounded average net fee rate (fee rate minus maker rebate rate), count the fee records, and show how far that average is from the simple mean of the account scope averages.
d.sql: WITH scope_fees AS (SELECT u.acctscope, COUNT(*) AS fee_record_count, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net_fee_rate FROM fees AS f JOIN orders AS o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users AS u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY u.acctscope) SELECT acctscope, avg_net_fee_rate, fee_record_count, ABS(avg_net_fee_rate - AVG(avg_net_fee_rate) OVER ()) AS distance_from_mean_scope_average FROM scope_fees ORDER BY acctscope;
